component-type.dataviz.$behaviour.dv-ren.$description: The CANDLESTICK TYPE PARTIAL for dv-render — open/high/low/close per period, one candle per session. Registered #260 as the second of the s259-D1 fast-follower types. OHLC is expressed as FOUR NAMED SERIES IN ORDER (open, high, low, close), which is the s249-D4 spec UNEXTENDED and is why the core's own writeTable emits exactly the columns the promoted snippet baked by hand — ds-027 (Dave, #100) makes that table THE accessibility answer, so it must not be able to drift from the chart. Enacts ds-027's SOLID TWO-STATE encoding (colour is close-vs-open and nothing else, both directions filled, --data-delta-gain/--data-delta-loss consumed verbatim; the #96-D1 ① hollow-up channel stays retired), the OHLC clause only this type can enforce (a high below its own open/close/low, or a low above them, THROWS by name), DV-D02 (every candle rides a g[data-fx][data-x0] that dv-behaviour TRANSLATES, so the 1px wick and the body width survive every container width) and DEF-003 (entry motion is CSS). ⚠ Computes its OWN domain and re-emits its OWN furniture: dv-render.js clamps `if (lo > 0) { lo = 0; }` AFTER calling fn.domain (dv-bar-009's zero baseline, right for a bar, catastrophic for a price series), so fn.domain cannot escape it — the same obstacle dv-render-line reported and dv-render-sparkline worked around. Core request filed at knowledge/_tmp/260/candlestick.core-requests.md. requires `data-dv-type="` — the same declaration every type partial owes.
